- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.23) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.16) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.16+); apply 1–2% downward bias for 30d forecasts.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizons; if forecast is > 2σ above recent mean, reduce by 1–2% per day until reversion.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated +0.23 spikes, model often fails to adjust for subsequent pullback; subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast 2–3 days after spike.
